situation: A business preparing for customer security audits next quarter.
complication: Three controls fall short of its own security policy.
key_question: Where do security controls fall short of policy, and what should be fixed first?

titles.situation: Three controls fall short of the business's security policy.
titles.options: Two ways to close the gaps before the audits.
titles.recommendation: Close sign-in and patching gaps first, then access reviews.
titles.roadmap: Fix exposure first, then complete reviews.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the controls meet policy.
titles.risks: The main risk is an attacker using a gap first.

issue_tree.finding: Some remote users sign in without the required second factor.
points: [F9] remote users have no multi-factor authentication.
issue_tree.so_what: This is the most direct route in for an attacker.

issue_tree.finding: Far more servers miss patches than policy allows.
points: [F6] of servers miss critical patches, [F8] over the limit.

hypotheses.text: Patching falls behind on a few server groups.

issue_tree.so_what: Patching must reach the policy limit before the audits.

chart.title: Servers missing patches against the policy limit.

options.name: Exposure first
options.description: Enforce multi-factor sign-in and clear critical patches, then finish access reviews.

options.name: All in parallel
options.description: Run all three fixes at once with equal priority.

recommendation.rationale: It closes the gaps an attacker can use soonest, then completes the reviews auditors will ask for; the chief information security officer decides.

actions: Enforce multi-factor sign-in for remaining remote users.
Patch the most exposed servers first.
Bring patching within the policy limit.
Complete access reviews for the remaining critical systems.
Collect evidence for the customer audits before next quarter.

risks.mitigation: Enrol users before enforcement and staff the help desk.
Test patches on a small group of servers first.
